papers.title_in_file: The Design and Implementation of a Quantum Information Science Undergraduate Program
papers.what_it_is: A program-design report from Universite de Sherbrooke on creating a 3.5-year co-op undergraduate degree in quantum information science aimed at training quantum software developers.

existing.note: Value matches Section 6. The paper gives no survey instrument, response count or scores behind 'overwhelmingly positive'.
Value matches Section 2.2.1; the study is reference [6], cited and not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that close to 50 interviews were conducted in 2020, 30 with representatives from large companies and startups, both local and international, and 20 with members of the student community.
quotes: close to 50 interviews were conducted back in 2020, 30 with representatives from large companies and startups, both local and international, and 20 with members of the student community.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; no interview protocol detail beyond the four questions and appendix summary.

assertions.value: The authors state that the interviewees were unaware of the intention to focus on quantum software, and that the questions were asked as generally as possible to gather unbiased insights.
quotes: Importantly, the interviewees were unaware of the intention to focus on quantum software.
These questions were asked as generally as possible to gather unbiased insights.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' description of their own method, without a test of bias.
assertions.reader_inference: No evidence is given that the interviews were free of bias; the statement describes intent.

assertions.value: The authors report that the industry interviews gave as required competencies programming skills (good code structure), project management, teamwork abilities and a solid foundation in quantum related fields.
quotes: Required competencies to work in the quantum industry include programming skills (good code structure), project management, teamwork abilities and a solid foundation in quantum related fields, highlighting the need for multidisciplinarity.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the interviews named robust coding skills, a multidisciplinary approach, a problem-driven mindset, project management and teamwork abilities as the most challenging skills to find.
quotes: The most challenging skills to find are robust coding skills, a multidisciplinary approach, problem-driven mindset, project management and teamwork abilities.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the interviews found the current lack of talent justifies hiring undergraduate degree holders, especially for larger companies, while start-ups tend to prefer candidates with a very specific expertise.
quotes: The current lack of talent in the field justifies hiring undergrad holders, especially for larger companies, while start-ups tend to prefer candidates with a very specific expertise.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the interviews found internships valuable but less beneficial if limited to only four months, and that longer internships should be privileged for deeper learning and contribution.

assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the student interviews identified characteristics of an attractive program: multiple potential career paths, a strong emphasis on practical training and cross-cutting professional skills.
quotes: These interviews identified characteristics of an attractive program, including multiple potential career paths, a strong emphasis on practical training and cross-cutting professional skills.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors report from the student interviews that science programs generally leave little room for the development of practical skills, and that internships are clearly seen as an essential part of the training program.

assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one interview study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the combined industry and student interview findings shaped three guiding principles: train a new generation of interdisciplinary scientists, implement an innovative and interdisciplinary pedagogical approach, and provide a professional, student-centered, training program.
quotes: The combined findings from industry and student interviews shaped three guiding principles for the undergraduate program in QIS:
Train a new generation of interdisciplinary scientists (Section 3);
Provide a professional, student-centered, training program (Section 4).

assertions.value: The authors state that the degree is focused on quantum software development, because they believed that existing programs in physics and engineering provided sufficient training opportunities in quantum computing hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that Universite de Sherbrooke began addressing the workforce problem in 2019 and launched the program in the fall of 2022.

assertions.value: The authors state that before the program a PhD, mainly in physics, was the primary way to join the quantum workforce in Sherbrooke, that a PhD student typically dedicates nearly a decade to higher education, and that no undergraduate program at the university clearly prepared students for software-oriented roles in quantum technology.

assertions.value: The authors state that in Quebec students go through two years of CEGEP after five high school years before university, and that science undergraduate programs typically last 3 years, often extended to 3 ½ years for the coop regime and 4 ½ years for coop engineering programs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the integrative project courses have significantly enhanced students' teamwork and overall communication skills, which they say demonstrates the effectiveness of the mechanisms put in place to foster these competencies.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper outlines the creative process and implementation of the program; the paper reports no graduate outcomes, since the first cohort has so far completed only its first mandatory internship.
quotes: we have outlined the creative process behind the development of the Quantum Information Science undergraduate program at Université de Sherbrooke, along with its implementation.
the first cohort has ended their first mandatory internships
assertions.certainty_reason: A scope statement read from the conclusion; the absence of outcome data is the reader's reading of the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cannot yet show that graduates are ready to join the quantum workforce, as the abstract says; the program had no graduates at the time of writing.
